title: Accessibility essentials
summary: Add alternative text, accessible names, and a sensible heading hierarchy.

scenario.briefing: The product page has images without descriptions, an icon button with no name, and headings that skip levels. Fix the markup so assistive technology can navigate and announce it.

hints: Every meaningful image needs alt text.
Keep one h1 and use h2 for sections.
Add alt to both images, aria-label to the cart button, and keep the h1 followed by h2 headings.

misconceptions.description: Giving every image an empty alt, including meaningful ones.
misconceptions.testDescription: Product images have descriptive alternative text.
misconceptions.feedback: Empty alt marks an image as decorative. Product images carry information and need a description.

misconceptions.description: Assuming a visible icon is enough to name a control.
misconceptions.feedback: An icon without a text alternative has no accessible name. Add aria-label or visible text.

sections.title: Alternative text
sections.body: Alternative text conveys the purpose of an image. Decorative images use an empty alt. Meaningful images describe what the image communicates in context.

sections.title: Accessible names
sections.body: Every interactive control needs an accessible name. Icon-only buttons use aria-label. Visible text inside a button also works.

sections.title: Heading hierarchy
sections.body: Headings create an outline. Use one h1 per page and nest h2 and h3 in order so screen reader users can navigate by headings.

vocabulary.definition: The label assistive technology announces for a control.
An image that conveys no information and uses empty alt.
The nested structure of h1 through h6 elements.

steps.title: Accessibility claims
hints: Check whether each statement treats accessibility as built into markup.
Empty alt is for decorative images only.
Select alt text, aria-label, and heading order; reject icon-as-name.

statements.label: Meaningful images need descriptive alternative text.
An icon-only button is accessible without an accessible name.
Headings should follow a logical order for navigation.
Empty alt is appropriate for decorative images only.

steps.explanation: Accessibility is carried by markup: alternative text, accessible names, and a logical heading outline.

accessibility.summary: The editor and preview are keyboard accessible, and HTML tests report text results.
